subject: Duplicate ingestion charges after migration — request for credit and tax guidance
messages:
From: Sara Patel <sara.patel@brightleaf.co>
To: Maya Srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Duplicate ingestion charges after migration — request for credit and tax guidance

Hi Maya,

Hope you’re well — following our migration on July 28th we saw a large unexpected ingestion spike that appears to have been billed in July (invoice BL-202607). Our engineering team attached a usage extract that shows duplicate events for a three-hour window (IDs 23-26 in the CSV). The net overage on that invoice is $12,340.

We’d like to request a credit for the duplicate usage. Two quick asks: 1) can you confirm you can apply a goodwill/service credit rather than a cash refund; and 2) what will the tax treatment be for the UK (VAT) — do you issue a credit memo net of VAT or do we need documentation for our VAT reclaim?

I’ve attached the usage slice and the invoice for reference. Need to resolve by end of month for our finance close — can you advise the timeline?

Thanks,
Sara Patel
Head of Platform Ops
BrightLeaf Analytics
Attachments: brightleaf-usage-slice.csv, invoice-BL-202607.pdf
From: Maya Srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwood.com>
To: Sara Patel <sara.patel@brightleaf.co>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 11:04:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Duplicate ingestion charges after migration — request for credit and tax guidance

Hi Sara — thanks for the heads up and for sending the slices. I’ve looped in Monica (Finance) and David (Customer Success) so we can validate usage and propose a remediation path.

Immediate next steps from our side:
- David will triage the usage export against our ingestion logs to confirm duplicate events and the time window.
- Monica will scope accounting treatment options (credit memo vs refund) and advise on VAT handling for the UK.
- I can provisionally hold any collections activity for BL-202607 while we investigate.

Can you confirm whether BrightLeaf prefers a credit memo applied to a future invoice or a one-off credit note showing the adjustment? Also, if you need any signed statements from your side (e.g., confirmation that the spike was caused by our migration guidance), let us know.

Thanks — I’ll come back with an ETA once David and Monica confirm.

Best,
Maya Srinivasan
Account Manager, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Sara Patel <sara.patel@brightleaf.co>
To: Maya Srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 08:23:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Duplicate ingestion charges after migration — request for credit and tax guidance

Hi Maya,

Appreciate the quick triage. BrightLeaf prefers a credit memo applied to the next invoice — we want the adjustment visible in our AR schedule. For VAT: BrightLeaf is UK-registered (VAT GB345678901). We generally net vendor credits against invoices; the VAT on the original invoice was charged at 20%. If you issue a credit memo, we will apply it gross against BL-202608 and treat the VAT reduction accordingly. If you instead issue a cash refund, we will require a formal tax adjustment.

Attached is a short note from our tax lead calling out the invoice lines where duplicates appear.

Thanks,
Sara
Attachments: brightleaf-usage-slice.csv (updated)
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Maya Srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 14:45:00 -0400
Subject: Internal: Draft credit memo and accounting treatment for BrightLeaf

Team — David’s check against the ingestion logs confirmed an automated retransmit during the post-migration window; clearly duplicate token counts for 2026-07-28 03:13–06:40 UTC.

Recommendation (Finance):
- Issue a goodwill/service credit memo for $12,340 (gross), to be applied to BL-202608.
- Credit memo will mirror the original invoice line items; VAT reduction will be reflected on the credit memo at 20% to align with BrightLeaf’s reconciliation process.
- No cash refund; we’ll apply as an AR credit.

Accounting actions required:
1) Create credit memo BL-CM-202608-01 (draft attached).
2) Post reversing journal entries against revenue for July (journal stub referenced in Drive link).
3) Route the credit memo to Tax for sign-off on EU/UK VAT reverse charge vs. adjustment (Irene — can you confirm?).

Irene: please confirm if any additional documentation is needed for VAT reclaim (e.g., supplier statement). If tax is satisfied, we can issue the credit memo on 2026-08-20.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Senior Manager, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
Attachments: credit-memo-draft.pdf
From: Maya Srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwood.com>
To: Sara Patel <sara.patel@brightleaf.co>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Aug 2026 17:38:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Duplicate ingestion charges after migration — request for credit and tax guidance

Hi Sara — quick update and confirmation:

- We will issue a goodwill credit memo (BL-CM-202608-01) for $12,340 on 2026-08-20. The credit will be applied to invoice BL-202608 as requested.
- The credit memo will reflect a 20% VAT reversal consistent with the original invoice; tax has been routed to Irene and she confirmed no additional supplier statement is required for your reclaim.
- Collections hold: we have placed BL-202607 on hold so there won’t be any collection outreach related to this amount.

Next steps for BrightLeaf: you should see the credit on BL-202608 and in your AR report within 24 hours of issuance. Monica copied Finance for posting and journal reversal. I’ve attached the credit memo draft for your records; we’ll send the formal credit memo PDF from billing once posted.

If anything changes or you need us to issue a separate invoice-level note for your VAT team, let me know — otherwise we’ll proceed as above.

Best regards,
Maya Srinivasan
Account Manager, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
Attachments: credit-memo-draft.pdf
